standard.title: Irregular Adjectives (beau, nouveau, vieux)
standard.explanation: Three common French adjectives are irregular and have special forms before masculine singular nouns that begin with a vowel or silent 'h'. These are: 'beau' (beautiful), 'nouveau' (new), and 'vieux' (old). Before a masculine noun starting with a consonant, use 'beau,' 'nouveau,' 'vieux.' Before a masculine noun starting with a vowel or silent 'h,' use 'bel,' 'nouvel,' 'vieil.' Feminine forms are: 'belle,' 'nouvelle,' 'vieille.' Plural forms are: 'beaux/belles,' 'nouveaux/nouvelles,' 'vieux/vieilles.' Examples: 'un bel homme' (a handsome man), 'un nouvel ami' (a new friend), 'un vieil arbre' (an old tree).

drills.question: Complétez: '___ homme.'
drills.explanation: Before a masculine noun starting with a vowel, use 'bel.' 'Un bel homme' = 'A handsome man.'

drills.question: Un ___ ami.
drills.explanation: Before a masculine noun starting with a vowel, use 'nouvel.' 'Un nouvel ami' = 'A new friend.'

drills.question: Quelle phrase est correcte?
drills.explanation: 'Un vieil arbre' is correct. Before a masculine noun starting with a vowel, use 'vieil.'

drills.question: Une ___ maison.
drills.explanation: Before a feminine noun, use the feminine form 'belle.' 'Une belle maison' = 'A beautiful house.'

drills.question: Complétez: '___ voiture.'
drills.explanation: Before a masculine noun starting with a consonant, use 'nouveau.' 'Un nouveau' = 'A new car.'

advanced.title: Irregular Adjectives — beau/bel/belle, nouveau/nouvel/nouvelle, vieux/vieil/vieux + Agreement
advanced.explanation: The adjectives 'beau,' 'nouveau,' and 'vieux' are classified as shoe verbs because their multiple forms fit into a pattern based on consonant/vowel beginnings of the following noun. Masculine singular forms: 'beau' + consonant (un beau garçon), 'bel' + vowel/silent h (un bel enfant, un bel homme). Feminine singular: 'belle' (une belle femme). Masculine plural: 'beaux' (les beaux garçons). Feminine plural: 'belles' (les belles femmes). The same pattern applies to 'nouveau' and 'vieux.' Note: 'vieux' is invariant in the masculine plural (les vieux livres = les vieux amis). These adjectives typically precede the noun (unlike most French adjectives, which follow). Gender and number agreement must always match the noun: 'une bel femme' is incorrect; it must be 'une belle femme.'

drills.question: Les ___ arbres sont dans le parc.

drills.question: Complétez: 'Une ___ hôtel n'existe pas; c'est 'Un ___ hôtel.'
drills.explanation: Masculine nouns use 'nouvel' (before vowel), feminine use 'nouvelle.' Gender agreement is critical.
